Date the tenant moved into the premises, distinct from legal tenancy commencement.
Date occupancy ended; distinguish from a written lease end date.
Expiration date of original lease, not most recent renewal.
Lease provision allowing the specified owner/family termination or tenant written agreement to termination.
Date possession actually returned to landlord, relevant to move-out photography and damage interval.
Whether any tenant from the prior tenancy remains in lawful possession when the new tenancy begins.
Public-housing lease covenant concerning controlled drugs/other illegality, federal conformity, in-effect-at-lease-start fact and substantial breach by tenant/household/guest.
Whether lease reserves a right of reentry for the specified breach.
Date the current tenancy or lease was renewed.
Relevant renewal date for the exemption-notice placement rule.
Monthly rent actually in effect when termination notice was served.
Rental debt amount at the legally relevant demand/eviction date.
Contractual interval between rent payment days, distinguishing less than three months from three months or more.
Whether tenant is manager being replaced with another manager; whether only compensation is free/reduced rent.
Beginning of tenant right to occupy for post-January 1, 2003 cleaning paragraph.
Actual consecutive occupancy days by the same tenant in this unit; used only where source imposes elapsed occupancy.
Whether the prescribed §98.0703(l) written exemption statement was delivered and whether it is included in the lease; retain commencement and renewal dates.
Service member intends to and does reside in property, residency start and rent arrears during first six months.
Date tenancy and right to occupy begin; source requirements sometimes expressly use right-to-occupy date.
Date this tenancy commenced; distinct from construction, notice, execution or move-out date.
First day of the tenancy, not the source retrieval or query date.
Initial rental tenancy start, including subtenancy where source specifies.
Start date of the tenancy, distinct from tenant occupancy duration and property age.
Whether the tenant remains in the specific unit when successor liability or an occupancy-credit alternative is evaluated.
Consecutive days in the rental term, for the seasonal deposit subsection.
Lease term length in months for the six-month advance-rent allowance.
Actual legal tenancy termination date relevant to the rule.
Legally effective termination, early departure without legal cause, lease-required notice, rerental date, lease expiry and remaining possession.
Whether hotel/motel/guesthouse occupancy is transient or seasonal under applicable law; do not import the 125-day deposit definition.
At-will, year-to-year, month-to-month or other tenancy classification.
Written lease, tenancy at will, lawful occupancy, post-foreclosure occupancy, or other status; tenancy at will and written-lease branches are distinct.
Number of tenants occupying unit who share relocation payment; not household size or number of units.
Whether cost is in base rent; whether separately metered; lease requires account in tenant name; petition/evidence/party agreement for ceiling adjustment.
Date tenant vacated premises; starts 21-calendar-day accounting clock.
Whether the particular lease or rental is for vacation or recreation.
Written lease authorization for reasonable attorney fees and treatment of late charges as rent.
Date an identified person told this owner of need for wheelchair-accessible unit, measured against preceding 12 months.
Whether the disability-related need is already obvious or known to provider.
Adult tenants residing in unit and adult tenants named in lease at termination; distinguish occupants from default check payees.
Age of the relevant applicant/person at the conduct date; compare minor/older-person branches without substituting owner age.
Tenant age at the specific legally relevant date; conversion law uses age before recording, not current age.
Tenant age at the source-specified event date, especially termination-notice service; not necessarily current age.
Necessary service animal or emotional-support animal for disability equal housing opportunity; ESA does not require service-task training.
Written refusal by all tenants of property, date and any written rescission; refusal lasts six months.
Whether the presence of children would constitute hardship to the qualifying elderly or infirm resident.
Whether children occupy or will occupy the premises with the applicant or tenant.
Whether tenant alleges the rent charged is illegal and seeks the petition remedy.
Family income and contemporaneous county average per-person income for protected-tenancy threshold.
Record category, conviction/date/judicial relief, juvenile status, current conduct, relation to housing and safety risk; source does not specify conviction-age measurement method.
Actual relevant disability, blindness or deafness and any law-specific qualifying definition.
Disability/handicap and the actual housing access need; the required legal definition depends on the source provision.
Whether the tenant meets the particular disability/handicap definition incorporated by the rule; definitions differ by jurisdiction.
Disability limiting a major life activity, requested policy/practice change, and necessity for equal opportunity; request can be oral or indicated without special words.
Opposition, complaint, reporting, testimony, assistance, accommodation request or other protected fair-housing activity.
Whether tenant has received financial assistance through a State or federal program, including welfare or rental assistance.
Address tenant supplied for subdivision h mailings; if none, vacated unit is statutory fallback.
Whether hotel/motel occupant resides there continually.
Household includes children under 18 or relevant pregnancy/familial-status facts.
Household annual income for the relevant relocation determination.
Household income, household size, applicable area/year AMI and whether income is at or below 80% AMI.
Members residing/proposing to reside together, aggregate income and tenant-paid portion of subsidized rent.
Number of persons in the household for the applicable income threshold; distinct from tenants sharing a unit.
Whether the occupant is a mobilehome homeowner within the cross-referenced section 798.9 definition.
Lawful verifiable income source, program/subsidy type, payee and representative; record HUD-VASH-specific representative treatment where relevant.
Presence and count of minor dependent children, using the source-required federal-tax or household definition.
Relevant mitigation: disability/violence context, rehabilitation, elapsed time/age, sentence compliance, rental history, support, third-party written payer, and reasons current rent will be paid.
Whether tenant has a permanent residence elsewhere during this rental.
Protected characteristic(s) implicated by conduct; track familial status, disability and lawful-income source separately.
Actual, perceived, intersecting or associated protected characteristic and its causal relationship to the challenged action; retain the list in the particular legal clause.
Actual protected ground implicated by the housing conduct; each subsection has its own list, and an age exception does not excuse discrimination on another ground.
Whether person receives public assistance or tenant receives housing subsidy/rental assistance at relevant time.
Whether government rent subsidy is involved in the specific rental application, distinct from a deed-restricted affordable building.
Whether tenant receives rental subsidy/assistance, with program separately identified where law requires.
Available/unavailable rental history, credit history versus score, sufficient income, demonstrated historical rent burden, and lack versus poor credit.
Whether a resident of one apartment is at least 65, disabled or chronically ill; the resident need not be the owner.
Status as tenant, subtenant, lessee, sublessee, or other natural person entitled to lease residential rental property under SDMC 98.0702.
Tenant receives tenant-based Section 8 Housing Choice Voucher assistance, not merely any housing subsidy.
Tenant owns, keeps or obtains a service/guide dog within applicable definition; do not assume every pet/assistance animal is this category.
Service-member qualification under Military and Veterans Code section 400, with relevant dates; military affiliation alone is not a supplied legal definition.
Tenant seeks rent reduction because of building/apartment conditions.
Actual/prospective vacancy date, MassAbility notice date and 15-day restricted-leasing window.
Whether request requires rent reduction, illegal drug use, direct threat to others, substantial physical property damage, or adding a nonexistent elevator; assess the actual request.
Requested change, communication/date, urgency, response, good-faith interactive process and equally effective alternatives.
Requested information, disability/need nexus and reliability/knowledge of third party or requester evidence; avoid collecting prohibited diagnosis/medical history.
Actor role and housing-related activity: landlord/owner, screening company, agent, public authority or other provider; distinguish admission, advertising, ongoing tenancy and termination.
Natural person/entity; owner/agent/representative/subcontractor; coordinator or its agent/representative/subcontractor.
Credit of last-month rent advance, accrued-interest handling, tenant notice and predecessor/successor compliance dates.
Actual bank interest received, accrued interest, last month covered by the advance, annual payment dates and amounts.
Number of rent months paid in advance under the particular advance-rent arrangement.
Actual/threatened reprisal or receipt of termination/rent-increase/substantial-terms-change notice, motive, notice date and nonpayment reason.
Landlord and ALL adult tenants written agreement: recipients, allocation percentages, each tenant delivery method/address and designated financial account.
Offer of the applicant-controlled alternative, election, lawful/verifiable evidence, reasonable response time and consideration in lieu of credit history.

Tacit or express agreement among rental property owners restricting competition concerning residential units under section4(b); do not require the narrower parallel-price-manipulation test for every agreement.
Actual reason for refusing applicant; whether refusal was because service-member rule prevents higher small-owner deposit.
Application materials, websites, and locations controlled by housing provider frequently visited by applicants.
Entity/individual requesting residential rental OR agreeing to be guarantor/cosignor.
Person considered for or requesting consideration for tenancy in a rental dwelling unit.
Fee demand/acceptance/payment, amount, charging party, date and application purpose.
Application complete/submitted/received/considered dates/order, written criteria delivered with form, qualification, first qualified applicant, selection/denial reason and selection date.
Whether the prospective tenant application for occupancy was approved.
Whether fee-based rental-finding business, broker license/section 87PP status, originally engaging party, contracting party, and tenant-side or landlord-side services.
Whether landlord offers money/other consideration for tenant to vacate; offer/disclosure/execution dates, terms, and whether this settles a pending unlawful-detainer action.
Whether inadvertent charge resulted from concurrent submissions, unconsidered application, refund date, offered transfer to another unit and applicant discretionary election.
Condition at inception, existing defects, ordinary/cumulative wear, tenant/guest/licensee damage and restoration evidence.
Condition statement contents, signature, print format, delivery and receipt dates; preserve tenant additions and landlord response dates.
Date offer contingent on later criminal-record inquiry or another lawful criterion was issued.
Reasonably needed verification request, disclosure/refusal/access permission, sensitive documents and return date.
Conversion type and proposed rent increase cost basis: solely conversion versus new service/amenity.
Recording date of relevant master deed, cooperative agreement or subdivision plat.
Nature/severity of conviction, elapsed time and specific relationship to tenancy ability and safety/property risk.

Identity of the alleged coordinator/service provider or principal; relationship to the separately assessed actor (purchasing owner/agent, coordinator itself, or coordinator agent/representative/subcontractor). Bind software/device/function and government-affordability status to that coordinator entity, not automatically to every assessed actor.
Receipt/subscription/contract/consideration for coordinator service, actual service functions and actor agency relationship.
Work description, time/rate, invoices/bills/receipts/provider identity/contact, materials routine purchase evidence, document receipt dates and good-faith estimates.
Whether provider uses or proposes to use credit history in the rental application.
Report obtained, subject applicant, landlord receipt date, delivery date/method and whether applicant presented it.
Advertisement/material/inquiry content, publication act, intent/knowledge, explicit versus indirect criminal-record limitations.
Whether inquiry, advertisement, selection, deposit, rent, tenancy termination or adverse action is based on criminal history, including a family member history.
Whether provider checks criminal history; record disposition, sealing/expungement, juvenile processing, blanket policy and conviction-linked decision.
Record disclosure recipients, expected evaluation use, actual use and purpose.
Violation, curability, prior written cure notice/deadline, whether cured and subsequent quit notice.
Date a particular payment was required or demanded.
Tenant displacement for demolition with replacement by new construction, project timing and applicable approvals.
Bank location, separate interest-bearing status, creditor protection, successor transfer terms and actual account handling.
Deposit receipt, institution/account data, annual interest payment, transfer to landlord/bank/account and notices/dates.
Whether security or funds securing future rent were collected for this tenancy.
Deposit terms for comparable applicants/tenants, charged amount and reason for difference; not just household presence or benefit receipt.
Damage beyond ordinary wear, lease sums due, amount withheld, itemization/delivery and actual tenancy termination.
Itemized proposed deductions, unpaid amounts, legal withholding, tax escalation, damage cause, reasonable repair amount and evidence.
Lease renewal/anniversary, interest amount, January31 written schedule election and payment/credit dates.
Kind of deposit violation: original notice, annual notice, unpaid required interest; tenant written demand, landlord cure/response and application-to-rent dates.
Existing deposit, proposed annual additional amount, monthly rent and date(s) of demand.
Deposit holding period measured from commencement, actual bank interest, annual statements, payment/deduction notices and accrued interest.
Payment receipt and later bank-account receipt contents, signatures and dates of delivery; these are separate duties.
Deposit records, damage and repair details, required receipts and condition statements, retention and requested office access.
Tenant/prospective tenant request, office/business hours and whether denial was wrongful.
Deposit and accrued-interest amounts actually transferred, successor receipt and written tenant notices.
Which precise section 15B subsection 6 clauses were violated, with dates and facts; not every deposit error triggers treble damages.
Tenant-funded necessary modification, landlord proof costly restoration, estimated restoration cost, affordable monthly installments and collected balance.
Actor, rental denial/terms/conduct, actual reason, and supporting evidence; protected status alone does not establish prohibited conduct.
Denial, terms, availability statement or other treatment linked to the specified protected ground.

Original statutory eviction ground/date; later residential re-rental offer date; tenant written opt-in date relative to termination notice; supplied and updated mailing/email address; written offer receipt/acceptance dates.
Tenant request date relative to statement receipt, and landlord receipt date; two separate 14-calendar-day clocks.
Tenant signature, date and substantial paragraph h(2) text; compare required termination notice or earliest fixed-term timing.
No-pet clause, denial, extra fee or damage claim related to service/guide dog.
Drug/alcohol test requirement or applicant consent request for treatment-facility information.
Whether current landlord received security OR rent electronically; for successor special branch whether successor personally received RENT electronically.
Date qualifying landlord employment ends.
Date of the particular agreement, notice, increase, demand or alleged conduct being evaluated; distinct from the query date.
Date of the transaction/conduct being assessed, distinct from the query date.
Specific fee/inquiry/report/refund event date rather than query date.
Creditor identity, title-transfer stage, initial communication/summons/complaint or pre-sale vacate request, written or verbal.
Foreclosing agency/new owner monetary written good-faith offer, initial/final notice, voluntary written acceptance, receipt date, five-day review acknowledgment, pressure tactics.
Date of completed foreclosure sale/acquisition, from which ten business days are counted.
Standard/advertised deposit, extra charged because credit/history/tenant factor, written reasons and lease-signing date, stated additional-deposit return date.
Actor role: owner, lessee/sublessee, broker, assignee, manager, rights holder, agent/employee or condominium/cooperative unit-owner organization as specified by the relevant subsection.
Landlord/owner/lessor/sublessor/assignee/agent or other person receiving or entitled to rents/benefits for rental-unit occupancy.
Correct amortization term for improvement as established under underlying program, not a chosen rate to optimize.
Financial/income standard used, rent denominator, aggregate household income treatment and comparison with married co-residents.
Tenant request/withdrawal, requested date, reasonable/mutually acceptable scheduling, inspection date, tenant presence, 48-hour notice and both-party signed waiver.
Whether establishing the wholly new tenancy initial rate or increasing an already established rent.
First lease signing, initial tenancy agreement or first-month rent tender, versus mere renewal.
Listed repair/cleaning deficiencies, text of b(1)-(4), delivery/inside placement and subsequent tenant cures.
Mutual agreement at commencement/during/after tenancy to email statement to tenant account or mail to supplied address.
Whether landlord elects the permissible accumulated-rent offset.
Ending/transfer date, voluntary status and nature of landlord interest transfer (sale, assignment, death, receiver or otherwise).
Prior written lease end date; owner written renewal/extension demand; tenant refusal; comparison of prior/proposed duration and provisions; legality of the proposed terms.
Requested price/rent range, all listed/held properties, offered showings and actual availability/listing representations.
Proposed move within park, reasonableness/necessity, emergency and notice dates, resulting damage, or sale-only demand to remove home.
Mobile-home sale, park-reserved purchaser approval and reason for withholding approval.
Actual date tenant vacated; distinct from notice service or proposed termination.
Representation/unsolicited contact, inducing/preventing rental purpose, neighborhood-entry characteristics and actual/constructive knowledge of association.
Written landlord notice, receipt date, reason, prescribed cure notification, and any similar notice received during prior 12 months.
Lease/agreement characterizes payment legally constituting security as nonrefundable.
Date the relevant notice was issued, distinct from service and receipt.
Actual service date of the relevant notice, not its drafting date or query date.
Date the particular termination, rent or other notice was served, identified by notice type; not query date.

Date the relevant Boston or Cambridge notice is given/delivered for the paired Guide duty, distinct from query date. Other statutory receipt-based clocks use their own transaction facts; do not infer receipt merely from service.
Date the relevant written Notice to Quit is served, not lease start or query date.
Contracted sale, buyer intent to personally occupy, requirement of vacant delivery at closing, and actual owner-occupancy intent.
Conditional-offer withdrawal, criminal-record basis, written reasons, date notified, appeal/correction/rehabilitation information.
Tenant vacancy date, intended occupant move-in date, consecutive primary residence duration, and any death after timely move-in.
Tacit/express agreement among2+independent owners to raise/change/maintain/manipulate prices of reasonably interchangeable NJ primary-residence units; includes coordinator-multiowner agreement.
Entrance fee, admission payment, compelled direct/indirect gift or donation to obtain park space.
Amount of the particular deposit, advance, fee, or other payment; character separately specified.
Legal purpose of payment, fee, deposit or charge: security/advance last-month rent, first-month rent, qualifying section 1950.6 screening fee, or other.
The legal purpose of the particular payment: security deposit, prepaid last-month rent, current rent, substitute fee, or another charge.
Actual date the landlord or agent received the specified payment.
Recipient, represented landlord, and whether recipient is landlord or landlord agent.
Number of persons engaging in/facilitating4(c) conduct; distinct from defined independent owner count.
Rental agreement authorizes security to restore/replace/return personal property or appurtenances and nature of default.
Ordinary pet restriction, pet rent or pet deposit proposed for the specific assistance animal; distinguish general security deposit.
Date capital-improvement petition was filed; selects imputed interest schedule independently from work commencement date.
Move-in, pre-work, and post-work photos with dates and unit identity.
Whether tenant possessions at inspection prevented identifying the specific later claimed repair/cleaning condition.
Date claimed condition arose after inspection; retain source ambiguity about stated interval endpoint.
Monthly rent, ordinary deposit, pet deposit, last-month rent or other prepaid funds securing future rent, and lease-inception payments.
Language primarily used, orally or in writing, to negotiate either the buyout agreement OR lease.
Damage, responsible person, consent/control, intent, ordinary wear, original condition list, later repair and renewed-damage evidence, repair/replacement cost.
Date and legal nature of the transfer of the landlord interest in this unit, excluding a mere mortgage grant.
Sale/transfer date, predecessor collected deposit/interest, whether funds actually transferred and successor identity.
Opposition, complaint, testimony, assistance, exercise/enjoyment of chapter rights or aiding others, and connection between adverse conduct and protected activity.
Current versus base/prior-year tax amounts, municipality-wide revaluation and first-year status, or REAP credit.
Tenant-designated bank account in writing, agreed available virtual method, or alternative written return arrangement; identify parties and timing.
Whether landlord elects registration-fee pass through; unit, amount, monthly installments, collection dates and underlying program eligibility.

Separate lawful rent at notice issuance, notice service and tenant vacancy; relocation paid, final-month rent due and waiver dates, reasonable moving expenses, other-law assistance and actual vacancy/continued possession.
Same/similar rental-unit availability now or prospectively and prior offer terms.
Work scope, permit requirements and copies, hazardous-material abatement contract if no permit, safety during occupancy, required consecutive vacancy and completion/start status.
Date rent is demanded; selects Berkeley FMR fiscal year.
Proposed amount, old/new rent, effective date, lease termination and continued-tenancy offer.
Date the proposed or challenged rent increase takes effect; selects lookback and CPI periods.
Effective date of the proposed rent increase.
Percentage of the challenged increase, with calculation basis retained; this source does not resolve aggregation or exactly-ten-percent treatment.
Tender/payment date, payee, full rent due, interest, suit costs and comparison with applicable deadline.
Notice/statement/advertisement text, publisher and protected preference it expresses; no automatic inference from tenant characteristic alone.
Notice, statement, advertisement or inquiry wording, person responsible, housing context and stated preference or questioned trait.
Combined repair AND cleaning deductions for $125 threshold, not total deposit, all deductions, or separate per-item caps.
Successor demand amount/date, earlier untransferred security, restitution/accounting completed before demand.
Specific requested modification/accommodation, necessity, reasonableness, payer, costs, effect on marketability and restoration proposal.
Offer terms/date received, tenant acceptance date, reoccupancy date and interest/contact details.
Required form, documented repayment agreements, assistance/court-order/eviction-restriction information, warning prominence and delivery proof.
Adverse housing action, actor, causal connection and dominant retaliatory purpose when the statute requires it.
Minimum screening criteria communicated in the written return offer, and the industry-accepted methods actually used.
Whether applicant supplies a screening report claimed reusable; legal qualification is a separate fact.
Effective termination date, deposit/interest, notice/location/hours, collection or redeposit, municipal officer availability and lawful deductions.
Residential rental owner or agent receiving application/fee; ownership definition distinct from unrelated screener.
Actual information-gathering out-of-pocket costs, reasonable value of time, reference/report work done and unused fee balance.
Amount paid/required, date, payee and purpose of buying consumer report and validating/reviewing/processing rental application; statutory refunds may apply despite label nonrefundable.
Whether charge meets section 1950.6 application-screening fee definition and requirements; labels alone do not decide legal character.
Applicant request date, withdrawal notice date, provider request receipt date, information relied on and response.
Blanket or individualized criminal review, credit score/history use, actual denial rationale, verification method and reviewer assignment.
Charge purpose, refund ability, amount, timing and whether applicant or existing tenant is charged.
Process offered WHEN fee collected: all-condition processA or full-unselected-refund processB.
Itemized expenses/time receipt, personal/mail delivery, email address and parties' email agreement.
Unused/full amount due, amount returned, refund date, selection/submission clocks and applicant fee-transfer choice.
Terminating tenant requests refund other than check payable to all adult tenants.
Initial itemized statement contents/delivery/tenant receipt date, remaining balance and actual refund date/method.
Amount/value of security including statutory security components, separately from first-month rent.
Purpose, amount, reasonableness, tenant/guest/licensee causation, cleaning or personal-property item, authorization and actual claim date.
Date security was demanded; distinguish from receipt, tenancy start and query date.
Whether and how much security deposit is held for this tenant, with collection and release dates.
Date security was actually collected.
Lawful deductions, remaining deposit amount transferred to successor or returned to tenant, accounting, tenant notice, successor receipt and investigation.
Proposed sublease total rent for the whole premises and independently lawful subletting/assignment authorization.
Written acknowledgment, lease disclosure, optional choice, agreed schedule and current choice to opt out.
Amounts, dates and agreed schedule of substitute-fee payments over the lease and all extensions.
Owner receipt date of municipal tax-reduction notice; selects schedule and November1 branch.

Residential tenant enforcement action, statutory-right exercise, authority report, written landlord complaint, union activity or specified unit-owner-organization rent payment/intention; record actor, dates and building connection.
Mutual agreement, tenant request, specified fee and structural/decorative/furnishing/similar alterations; whether actually cleaning/repair chargeable to previous tenant.

Asserted ground plus its substantiating facts, including actual default, material breach, nuisance, waste, criminal threat/activity, prohibited assignment, authorized entry refusal, unlawful use, ended employment/license, or tenant written notice/accepted surrender as applicable. A category label alone does not establish a ground.
Either party notice of intention to terminate: date, recipient and content.
Either party termination-intent notice, actual statutory provision, date provided and lease-ending context.
Decision not to renew, notice to quit/nonrenewal/expiration, summary-process initiation or demand that occupant leave; includes actor and dates.
Whether the valuation concerns qualifying uncompensated labor in a capital-improvement rent petition.
Actual unit availability now or within reasonable time, landlord actual/constructive knowledge, timing of fee demand.
Gross rates and effective dates over the preceding 12 months, identifying accepted discounts/concessions separately.
Date tenant actually vacated as a result of the stated eviction/retirement/personal-occupancy notice.
Specific lease/agreement clause and rights it purports to waive or conflict with; distinguish its existence from attempted enforcement.
Repair/cleaning start/end, reason reasonably impossible to complete in 21 days, and who performed work.
